title: automation (cluster): measure whether a published connector definition change materialises on every replica or only on the publishing one
body:
domain:server#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia

Filing gate: ② an unmeasured observation that a maintainer ruling ordered measured on its own card. Ruling 6513279565 on #27428, out-of-scope item: "the dev's earlier unmeasured observation (a published connector change may materialise only on the publishing replica) is measured after this lands, on its own card". #27428 landed as PR #27941 at 2026-10-30T05:52Z. ⛔ Not a claim.

## Question

#27941 added lane 4 (`connector-credential.mutated`) of the §6.2 cluster-invalidation family. Through it, a peer re-runs its connector reconcile when a **credential** is written. The open question is the **definition** side. When a connector instance's declared definition changes through a metadata publish on one replica, does every peer re-materialise it? The candidate paths are lane 1 (`metadata.changed`) or lane 2 (`metadata.mutated`) reaching the automation plugin's reconcile. The alternative is that only the publishing replica rebuilds, until a reload or restart.

## Wanted

- A two-kernel measurement over one store and one shared bus, built like #27941's `connector-credential-cluster.test.ts`. Publish a changed connector definition on node A and read node B's live instance.
- If B converges, pin that and close the card.
- If B does not converge, report which lane should carry the change, under the §6.2 principle of one signal and no second propagation channel (triage 6490140325). Do not build a fix without a ruling on that lane.

## Reader

`domain:server` (`service-automation`, `service-cluster`).

## Dedupe

#27428 / PR #27941 (credential lane). No open card covers definition propagation.
